# Independent audit of the attained normal-stress convex-order obstruction

Audited `candidate 6521ec5aae22f16f` and ran
`supporting computation verify_normal_hinge_convex_order_obstruction.py` successfully. The
classification and the stated scope pass. No mathematical correction
was needed.

## All geometric minimizers are covered

The four binary base points are extreme in the square, so the convex
hull has exactly the specified interval fibers. It is full dimensional
and has no additional integer fibers. Closed cap boundaries have zero
mixed length measure, while coverage still retains their points.

For a covered interval, the two-hinge lower bound one is valid with
either normal-sign pattern. A single cap covering the whole interval
costs at least two. Therefore any cover with a wholly covered fiber
costs at least five; the exhibited `17/4` excludes all such covers at
a global minimum, including endpoint and empty-cap degeneracies.

Every minimizing pair consequently has opposite signs and proper cuts
in every interval. The union has mass eight and the sum of the two cap
budgets is at most eight. Their intersection has zero length, so their
two affine thresholds agree on every fiber. Their common trace is
affine on the four square vertices. The checkerboard height array is
orthogonal to this entire affine trace space, not just to constants.
The exact squared-error decomposition therefore makes the zero trace
the unique global minimizer. The cap budgets additionally force its
affine trace sum to be zero, but omitting that redundant restriction
from the lower-bound minimization cannot invalidate the argument;
the unique zero minimizer meets both budgets exactly.

## All normal joint stresses are covered

Each contact is uniquely `x_z=0` in the interior of its interval, so
the only dual cover weights are `(1/2,1/2)` and every section trace
density is one. Equal source/contact masses force the two budget
multipliers to agree. The zero-total/zero-base-moment kernel on the
four vertices is exactly the one-dimensional checkerboard space.
Thus all contact marginals, including the possibilities with zero
contact weights, have precisely the displayed form
`omega(z)=alpha+r+s epsilon_z`, `|s|<=alpha+r`.

Conversely every such nonnegative array with `alpha+r>0` satisfies the
full offset, base, continuous, sphere-normal, and certificate-weight
equations. The continuous equation is exact because the contact and
section first moments are zero and the two cap first moments equal
the signed hinge integrals. Hence the obstruction is not limited to
one conveniently chosen stress.

## Convex order and both normalizations

The test functions `max(0,1-q_p(z))` are globally convex because `q_p`
is globally affine. Their traces on the binary square are its four
vertex indicators. Convex-order domination between equal-mass measures
on these vertices therefore forces equality at every vertex. The two
normal source arrays differ by `2 alpha h_z`, so they cannot both
dominate the same contact array when `alpha>0`. The quantitative
deficit at least `alpha/4` follows by summing the two-source pointwise
minimum and then using the four-vertex pigeonhole bound.

For `alpha=0`, a uniform positive section stress does satisfy convex
order, exactly as the note states. The counterexample excludes all
NORMAL stresses, not all abnormal stresses.

The values `D_int=[-2,2]` and `D_all=[-5/2,5/2]` are exact. The two
extreme heights of the latter occur over the same real midpoint of
the square. Normalizing by `[-W,W]` scales every hinge by `1/W`, leaves
the geometric minimizers unchanged, and multiplies the proper section
coarea masses by `W`. Substituting `alpha+Wr` for `alpha+r` therefore
preserves the entire classification and convex-order obstruction.

## Scope

The cap budget is `tau=1/2`, and the two caps necessarily saturate it.
With only two covering caps, a strictly smaller budget for both would
violate the elementary union bound. The example therefore is NOT a
strict-feasibility counterexample for that fixed cap count. Its
dimension-specific OC target is `1/8`, and no sub-OC cap budget or
minimizing-body counterexample is asserted. It does refute the universal
normal source-to-contact convex-order conversion at an actual attained
hinge minimum, under either of the discussed affine width normalizations.
